procedural_matters: The technical committee was represented by Jan Schmidt (member of the technical committee).
The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: Races 4, 5 and 6 were sailed on Monday, 22 June 2026.
After race 6 on Monday 22 June 2026, the crew of GER 66 was instructed by the technical committee member to be weighed at 18:35 hrs.
The combined weight of the crew of GER 66 was 608,8 kg weighed at the floating pier.
After 45 minutes, at 19:10 hrs. the weighing in was performed again at the DSV, resulting in the combined weight of 602,4 kg.
The upper limit for the combined weight of the crew declared on the certificate is 590 kg, and the bottom limit is 460 kg.

SI 11.5 states the following: Penalties for breaches of class rules, RRS 50 or 78.1, class rules, rules in the Notice of Race or Sailing Instructions marked ‘[DP]’ or [SP], should the case go to a hearing, are at the discretion of the international jury and may be less than a disqualification.
conclusions: GER 66’s combined weight of the crew exceeded the upper limit stated on the boat’s certificate, breaking ORC class rule 200.1(a).
By sailing with a combined crew weight above the upper weight limit declared in her certifcate and therefore not maintaining the boat to comply with her class rules, GER 66 broke RRS 78.1.
decision: Using the World Sailing Discretionary Penalty Guidelines for Boats & Support Persons a starting penalty of 20% was decided.
The penalty was increased because the breach was not accidental.
The penalty is a 30% discretionary penalty, calculated using the method described in rule 44.3(c) and applied to races 4, 5 and 6.
